questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Australia, and when I started researching courses and universities, I realised that the University of Melbourne is highly ranked and offers the most interesting classes. Furthermore, it was important for me to be able to travel and experience the country I was in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It was a bit much the first day, but then it became very easy. UniMelb's website has a lot of information, and any additional information was available at Stop 1

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had some help switching a class, but that was about it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I decided that I did not want to stress about housing and finding something just before the semester started, so I decided to accept UniMelb's offer for international students. I stayed at The Lofts, which was really awesome. I met a lot of other exchange students, and it just made it easy to meet people. Furthermore, you can only stay at The Lofts if you are a graduate student, which I found nice because of similar ages.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I stayed off campus, but it was right across the street from campus, so very close. But I know that some people who stayed further away from campus ended up spending quite a lot on public transport.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought it was nice to accept housing through UniMelb. It is expensive, but housing in Melbourne is just really expensive. I talked to some people who found housing on their own, and it seems like you have to be very lucky to find something cheap. Some people ended up paying the same as me, but living 45 minutes by tram away.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit early you could register, but there was also a secondary period for registrering for classes. I would, however, highly recommend registrering in the first period, as each subject have multiple classes, and you can prioritise which classes (regarding time) you want. This makes it easier to make a timetable that allows time for other things, except studying.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 is a very helpful service. On the first couple of days in the secondary registration period, they have full days where you can come unannounced and talk to them to get help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my classes, but ended up switching a class after I saw that it was recommended that I could speak/understand Chinese for one of my original classes. But it was easy to switch, so I ended up in all my preferred classes and my preferred timetable as well.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Registrer in the first period, even if it seems unmanageable. And maybe take some intense subjects? I had one that ended a month early, and one class that started a month later. It means that the teachings are going to be three hours instead of two, but I only had three weeks where I had four subjects.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had three MA classes and one third-year BA course. But ironically, the third-year BA course was the one I found most difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is a lot more class discussions at UniMelb than what I am used to at UCPH. Which, in some cases, was good, but in some cases was bad. Especially because not all students have the same English skills. However, the level is a bit lower at UniMelb, so I found it easier to show up without necessarily having done all the readings and still be able to follow along. All my classes also had compulsory attendance, so that was different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Race, Ethnicity, and Nationalism, 2)  Latin America in the World, 3)  Public Policy Lobbying Strategies, 4)  International Organisations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all my courses, but I would definitely recommend "International Organisations" as Justin is a really good teacher, and the course is interesting. Likewise, I would recommend "Latin America in the World" as there are a lot of different kinds of teachings, and you just learn a lot about Latin America.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The visa (!!!!). It is really expensive. It cost 7.571 DKK and I also had to buy an OSCH insurance that cost 2.034 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Of course, it costs something to move and get a blanket, pillows, etc., but if you go to Kmart, you can really get them cheaply. I was surprised by how cheap I found public transport, but I ended up walking most places anyway.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is everything. You can join sports clubs for most sports, clubs for wine drinking or chocolate eating, and cultural clubs like the French club, the German club, the Myanmar society, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining Mussex, as this society is for exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: As much as possible. I travelled the entire East Coast before the semester started and loved it. And then see if you can adjust your timetable so you can go on extended weekends to places in Australia. I also went on an Easter Holiday, so there are so many opportunities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In a lot of classes, there will be a lot of exchange students, but local students are also in the classes, so it is just a matter of finding them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I do not think I found anything particularly challenging, but it was definitely different from Denmark how outgoing Australians are, even if you are just going grocery shopping.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I actually came to really appreciate how outgoing and social Australians are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Remember to enjoy the social life - you just need to pass your subjects, and the level is lower 
2) Enjoy what Melbourne has to offer, as well as Australia 
3) It might seem like there are a lot of administrative things you need to do beforehand, but everything works out, and UniMelb is very good at helping.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience Australian culture while studying at such a prestigious university. And all the international friends I made, as we are planning on visiting each other next year.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe at first, being alone in such a big city, and knowing you know no one. And that you can not just call home if something happens, as the time difference is quite big.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
